message:
Now I understand the setup. The fuzzer passes the raw input bytes directly to `plist_from_json` with the exact size. The vulnerability is that `parse_primitive` calls `strtol` and `atof` on a non-null-terminated string. If the input ends with a primitive token (like a number) at the very end of the buffer, `strtol`/`atof` will read past the buffer boundary.

Let me check how the target is built and if there's a way to test locally. Let me look at the build setup.

<｜｜DSML｜｜parameter=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>ls /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libplist/ && echo "---" && find /workspace -name "*.sh" -o -name "Makefile" -o -name "CMakeLists.txt" | grep -v libfuzzer | grep -v honggfuzz | grep -v aflplusplus | head -20</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
